claims.text: Constituent count alone does not explain the deformation and failure differences between equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi and its subsets.
Mn affects magnetic interactions that control the fcc-to-hcp phase transformation in this alloy family.
Mn-free or Mn-reduced alloys such as CrCoNi have sufficiently reduced magnetic frustration to permit a deformation-induced fcc-to-hcp transformation.
CrCoNi has a lower-energy hcp state than its fcc state.
Dislocation slip and interactions with internal boundaries trigger the fcc-to-hcp transformation in CrCoNi.
The deformation-induced fcc-to-hcp transformation provides additional strain hardening through transformation-induced plasticity.
The fcc-to-hcp transformation increases ductility in CrCoNi.
Mn in equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi creates magnetic frustration that removes the energetic preference driving the fcc-to-hcp transformation.
Mn-induced magnetic frustration stabilizes the fcc structure and suppresses deformation-induced transformation in CrMnFeCoNi.
CrMnFeCoNi and CrCoNi can both begin as single-phase fcc solid solutions.
Identical thermomechanical processing produces comparable single-phase fcc initial microstructures in the quinary alloy and all tested subsets.
The extent of deformation-induced fcc-to-hcp transformation mediates differences in work hardening.
Stacking-fault and nanotwin formation mediates work hardening differences among the alloys.
Relative to CrMnFeCoNi, CrCoNi will have a higher work-hardening rate under identical deformation conditions.
Relative to CrMnFeCoNi, CrCoNi will exhibit higher tensile strength.
Relative to CrMnFeCoNi, CrCoNi will exhibit greater ductility.
Quaternary and ternary subsets generally exhibit more transformation activity and better work hardening than the quinary alloy.
The proposed mechanism applies at room temperature when deformation is sufficient to trigger phase transformation in initially single-phase fcc material.
Minor compositional variations and processing-induced defects could also influence the measured mechanical differences.
Comparable fcc-to-hcp transformation and work-hardening behavior in CrMnFeCoNi and the Mn-free or Mn-reduced comparator would falsify the proposed Mn-mediated explanation.

contradictions.description: The mechanism is restricted to Mn-free or Mn-reduced alloys and the evidence says the transformation occurs only in CrCoNi among the examined ternary derivatives, whereas the prediction broadly attributes enhanced transformation and properties to quaternary/ternary subsets as a class.
